o1.biggest_strength: Dissects the 4.0 into profit per segment against a 2.5 break-even, puts the price-mismatch feed fix first, and builds a budget that adds to exactly $240,000 with a reserve rule, a downside range, and a bold regional test to challenge the 1.2.
o1.biggest_mistake: Complicated to run: a reserve rule, a regional state-split test, and several simultaneous changes make week one hard to execute and the 13% reported-revenue drop may scare the CFO if not framed first.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Trim to the essential moves (feed fix, brand exclusion, reallocation), push the regional test to a later month, and state the revenue/profit trade-off even more plainly up front.

o2.biggest_strength: Cleanest read: brand is 11% of spend and 50% of value, PMax ex-brand is 2.03 and loses ~$36,700; a tidy split to $240,000, feed fix with concrete causes, and a usable title and ad copy rewrite.
o2.biggest_mistake: Forecast relies on an aggressive PMax jump to 2.6 and brand at 25 ROAS after the switch; the plan is competent but less ambitious, with no test to prove the broad spend isn't building future brand demand.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a way to test whether the 1.2 broad spend drives later brand demand, and show profit ranges per line rather than a single base case.

reason: Both are good and both would get used, but Output 1 goes further: it takes the 4.0 apart into profit per segment, fixes the feed first, gives a split that adds up, and has a downside range and a test, which is what I asked for. Output 2 is the cleaner read but a bit safer and more optimistic on the upside.
